module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Representations as $p + 2^x + 7 \cdot 2^y$ with $p \equiv 5 \pmod 6$

Number of ways to write the $n$-th positive odd integer in the form $p + 2^x + 7 \cdot 2^y$
with $p$ a prime congruent to $5 \bmod 6$ and $x, y$ positive integers.
$$a(n) = \left|\left\{(p, x, y) : p + 2^x + 7 \cdot 2^y = 2n - 1 \text{ with } p \text{ prime},
p \equiv 5 \pmod 6, x, y \in \mathbb{Z}^+\right\}\right|.$$

*References:*
- [A157225](https://oeis.org/A157225)
- Z.-W. Sun, "Mixed sums of primes and other terms", arXiv preprint
  [arXiv:0901.3075](https://arxiv.org/abs/0901.3075) [math.NT], 2009.-/

@[expose] public section

namespace OeisA157225

/-- Number of representations of $2n - 1$ as $p + 2^x + 7 \cdot 2^y$ with $p \equiv 5 \pmod 6$. -/
def a (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  if n = 0 then 0
  else
    let N := 2 * n - 1
    ∑ x ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N,
    ∑ y ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N,
      if 2 ^ x + 7 * 2 ^ y < N ∧
         (N - (2 ^ x + 7 * 2 ^ y)).Prime ∧
         (N - (2 ^ x + 7 * 2 ^ y)) % 6 = 5 then 1 else 0

/-- Value of the sequence `a` at 1. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_1 : a 1 = 0 := by decide

/-- Value of the sequence `a` at 2. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_2 : a 2 = 0 := by decide

/-- Value of the sequence `a` at 11. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_11 : a 11 = 1 := by decide

/-- Value of the sequence `a` at 12. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_12 : a 12 = 1 := by decide

/-- Value of the sequence `a` at 13. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_13 : a 13 = 0 := by decide

/-- Value of the sequence `a` at 14. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_14 : a 14 = 2 := by decide

/--
On Feb. 24, 2009, Zhi-Wei Sun conjectured that $a(n) = 0$ if and only if $n < 11$ or
$n \in \{13, 16, 992\}$; in other words, except for $25, 31, 1983$, any odd integer greater
than $20$ can be written as the sum of a prime congruent to $5 \bmod 6$, a positive power of $2$
and seven times a positive power of $2$.

Answer: false, for n = 716993899 we have a(n) = 0.
See T. Adamczewski, OEIS Open: How many conjectures can language models turn into theorems?,
[arxiv/2608.11941](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.11941).
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11,
  formal_proof using lean4 at
    "https://github.com/epoch-research/LeanOpenProblems-results/blob/main/runs/oeis-full-50usd-ant-j0j0g4uzligm1k41/oeis_157225_conjecture_0/Submission/Spec.lean"]
theorem conjecture (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) :
    a n = 0 ↔ n < 11 ∨ n = 13 ∨ n = 16 ∨ n = 992 := by
  sorry

end OeisA157225

findings.description:
The declaration is tagged `@[category research solved, formal_proof using lean4 at …]`, and its docstring says "Answer: false, for n = 716993899 we have a(n) = 0". But its Lean statement is still Sun's un-negated conjecture: `theorem conjecture (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) : a n = 0 ↔ n < 11 ∨ n = 13 ∨ n = 16 ∨ n = 992`, i.e. `∀ n, 0 < n → (a n = 0 ↔ …)`. That proposition is false. So the file records a false statement as a solved, formally proved theorem.

The linked formal proof (`oeis_157225_conjecture_0.disproof`) proves `¬ ∀ (n : ℕ), A157225 n = 0 ↔ n < 11 ∨ n = 13 ∨ n = 16 ∨ n = 992`. That is the negation, so it does not imply the repository statement (PROOFS.md check 2 fails).

I refuted the statement in Lean using only the standard axioms (scratch file /workspace/review/scratch4.lean).
- `a_eq_aFast : a n = aFast n` restricts the exponent ranges from `Icc 1 N` to `Icc 1 (Nat.log 2 N)`, via `Finset.sum_subset` and `Nat.lt_pow_succ_log_self`.
- `aFast 716993899 = 0` is proved with `interval_cases x <;> interval_cases y` over x, y ≤ 30, closing each case by `decide` or `norm_num` (compositeness).
- Together these give `conjecture_false_kernel : ¬ ∀ n : ℕ, 0 < n → (a n = 0 ↔ n < 11 ∨ n = 13 ∨ n = 16 ∨ n = 992)`. `#print axioms` reports only `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`.
- In a second scratch file, `OeisA157225.conjecture 716993899 (by norm_num)` together with `a 716993899 = 0` derives `False`.

The definition `a` and the biconditional are otherwise faithful to the OEIS comment. `a` matches the OEIS b-file for every n ≤ 200000, the zeros there are exactly {1,…,10, 13, 16, 992}, and all six `test` values agree. The only defect is the polarity under the solved tag. When commit #5114 changed the tag from open to solved and added the disproof link, it did not negate the statement.
findings.source_evidence:
OEIS A157225 (entry text read via the oeisdata mirror, revision #14, Aug 20 2026): "Adamczewski disproved the above conjecture using n = 716993899, a(n) = 0, in linked article. - _Michael De Vlieger_, Aug 20 2026".

arXiv:2608.11941 (T. Adamczewski, OEIS Open), settled_conjectures_table.tex, A157225 row: "Disproved. A counterexample is n=716993899: a(n)=0, although n is neither below 11 nor one of the three listed exceptions."

The linked Spec.lean states `theorem oeis_157225_conjecture_0.disproof : ¬ ∀ (n : ℕ), A157225 n = 0 ↔ n < 11 ∨ n = 13 ∨ n = 16 ∨ n = 992`.

Repository convention (CONTRIBUTING.md): "If the problem has been solved to the negative, then `P` should be replaced with `¬ P`." The sibling files citing the same paper or run set (OEIS/306477, 60841, 64169, 84046, 46969, 1223) and OEIS/303639 all use `¬ ∀ …`, and OEIS/70823 uses `answer(False) ↔ …`. Past fix PR #1334 flipped `answer(True)` to `answer(False)` on a negatively solved Erdős problem and was labelled misformalization.

review.notes:
The file has one real defect, and it comes from commit #5114 ("Mention recently solved conjectures"). That commit changed `conjecture` from `research open` to `research solved`, added the disproof link and wrote "Answer: false" in the docstring, but left the statement un-negated. The two other files changed in that commit (129365, 3625) had positive answers, so keeping their statements was right there.

The rest of the file is faithful:
- `a` (a double sum of indicators over x, y ∈ [1, 2n−1]) equals the source's count of triples (p, x, y), because p is determined by (x, y) and terms outside the range vanish. I proved the range reduction `a = aFast` in Lean and checked `aFast` against the whole 200000-term b-file with no mismatches.
- The tests a_1, a_2, a_11, a_12, a_13, a_14 match the b-file.
- The hypothesis `0 < n` matches the OEIS offset 1.

Because this is a single root cause, the same issue is reported as a finding (the statement must be negated) and cross-listed under status_issues (the formal_proof record is contradicted by its own linked proof). It needs one fix.

Minor, not reported as findings:
- The formal_proof URL points at `blob/main`, not a pinned commit.
- The docstring of `a` says "with p ≡ 5 (mod 6)" and omits "prime" and "x, y positive"; the module docstring and the Lean code are complete.

Scratch files are in /workspace/review/:
- scratch2.lean: refutation using `native_decide`.
- scratch3.lean: b-file comparison.
- scratch4.lean: kernel-only refutation, `#print axioms` = [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound], compiles in about 2–3 minutes.
- scratch5.lean: derives `False` from the repository's `conjecture`, and checks that the suggested fixed statement typechecks.

demonstrated.claim: The declaration's exact statement (`¬ type_of% @OeisA157225.conjecture`) is refuted using only the standard axioms: `OeisA157225.a 716993899 = 0` is checked in the kernel (exponents above 30 overshoot N = 1433987797, and the 30×30 remaining pairs fail by size, residue mod 6, or `norm_num` compositeness), yet 716993899 is neither < 11 nor in {13, 16, 992}, so this `research solved` theorem is false as stated and should be negated.

submission.summary:
`/workspace/review/trivial_proof.lean` imports `FormalConjectures.OEIS.«157225»` and has two parts:
- `a_716993899 : OeisA157225.a 716993899 = 0` is proved on the file's own definition. Exponents of 31 or more exceed N = 2·716993899 − 1 = 1433987797 < 2^31. The remaining 900 pairs (x, y ≤ 30) are closed by `decide` (size or residue mod 6) or by `norm_num` (the candidate is composite).
- `conjecture_is_false : ¬ type_of% @OeisA157225.conjecture` follows in three lines, since the counterexample is neither below 11 nor one of 13, 16, 992.

`#print axioms` reports only `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`: no `sorry` and no `native_decide`. The file compiles in about 6 seconds with no errors or warnings.

Two sanity checks were run in a separate scratch file:
- `rfl` confirms that `type_of% @OeisA157225.conjecture` is literally `∀ n, 0 < n → (a n = 0 ↔ n < 11 ∨ n = 13 ∨ n = 16 ∨ n = 992)`.
- The same tactic script, run at n = 716993900, fails on exactly 42 pairs where the remainder is a prime ≡ 5 (mod 6). That matches a count of 42 computed independently, so the case split really checks every pair.

This shows that the declaration, tagged `research solved` with a `formal_proof` link to a disproof, asserts a false proposition. It should be negated.

trivial_proof.lean:
import FormalConjectures.OEIS.«157225»

/-! `OeisA157225.conjecture` is tagged `research solved` (with a `formal_proof` link to a
*disproof*), but it still states Sun's conjecture un-negated, and that statement is false. -/

-- Counterexample: `OeisA157225.a 716993899 = 0`, i.e. N = 2·716993899 − 1 = 1433987797 is not
-- p + 2^x + 7·2^y with p prime ≡ 5 (mod 6), x, y ≥ 1. Exponents ≥ 31 overshoot N < 2^31; the
-- 30 × 30 remaining pairs fail by size, by residue mod 6, or by compositeness (`norm_num`).
theorem a_716993899 : OeisA157225.a 716993899 = 0 := by
  rw [OeisA157225.a, if_neg (by norm_num)]
  refine Finset.sum_eq_zero fun x hx => Finset.sum_eq_zero fun y hy => if_neg ?_
  rintro ⟨h1, h2, h3⟩
  obtain ⟨hx1, -⟩ := Finset.mem_Icc.mp hx
  obtain ⟨hy1, -⟩ := Finset.mem_Icc.mp hy
  have hpx : 0 < 2 ^ x := by positivity
  have hpy : 0 < 2 ^ y := by positivity
  have hx30 : x ≤ 30 := by
    by_contra hc
    have := Nat.pow_le_pow_right (show 0 < 2 by norm_num) (show 31 ≤ x by omega)
    omega
  have hy30 : y ≤ 30 := by
    by_contra hc
    have := Nat.pow_le_pow_right (show 0 < 2 by norm_num) (show 31 ≤ y by omega)
    omega
  clear hpx hpy hx hy
  revert h2
  interval_cases x <;> interval_cases y <;> first
    | exact absurd h3 (by decide)
    | exact absurd h1 (by decide)
    | (intro h2; exact absurd h2 (by norm_num))

-- `OeisA157225.conjecture` (a `research solved` theorem) is FALSE exactly as the file states it:
-- n = 716993899 > 0 has `a n = 0`, yet it is neither < 11 nor one of 13, 16, 992.
theorem conjecture_is_false : ¬ type_of% @OeisA157225.conjecture := by
  intro h
  have := (h 716993899 (by norm_num)).mp a_716993899
  omega

#print axioms conjecture_is_false

submission.summary:
I edited only FormalConjectures/OEIS/157225.lean. The lakefile.toml and run/ changes that git status shows were already there before I started.

`OeisA157225.conjecture` now states the negation of Sun's conjecture: `theorem conjecture : ¬ ∀ n : ℕ, 0 < n → (a n = 0 ↔ n < 11 ∨ n = 13 ∨ n = 16 ∨ n = 992) := by sorry`. This follows the repository convention for problems solved in the negative, so the `research solved` tag and the `formal_proof` link now describe a true statement. The proof stays `by sorry`, because the formal-proof linter requires that for `formal_proof`-tagged statements.

The linked Lean theorem implies the new statement. It proves `¬ ∀ n, A157225 n = 0 ↔ …`, where `A157225` counts the same pairs as `a`, and at n = 0 the biconditional holds anyway.

Edits that go with the fix:
- The docstring line "Answer: false, for n = 716993899 we have a(n) = 0." now reads "This is false: $a(716993899) = 0$, although $716993899$ is neither below $11$ nor one of $13, 16, 992$." The conjecture text and the arXiv:2608.11941 reference are unchanged.
- The formal_proof URL is pinned from blob/main to commit fd09021e79869476ef83cda231312f1a2a89c8d7 with anchor #L54, as in the sibling OEIS files. I checked that the file at that commit is byte-identical to main and that the URL returns HTTP 200.

The definition `a`, the six test theorems and the category/AMS attributes are unchanged.

Checks:
- The prescribed `lake env lean --json` command reports only `declaration uses 'sorry'`.
- With the FormalConjectures library's lint options passed as -D flags, it reports nothing.
- In a copy of the edited file outside the checkout (/workspace/review/fixed_check.lean), `theorem conjecture_check : type_of% @conjecture` is proved from `a 716993899 = 0`. That lemma is proved by a case split over x, y ≤ 30 closed with `decide`/`norm_num`, with no `native_decide`. `#print axioms` reports only [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound], so the corrected statement is true as declared.
